items.name: Sequence as developmental engine
items.description: Ascending or descending sequences of 3–4 repetitions move the music forward. The sequence is harmonically directed (circle-of-fifths, descending thirds, ascending seconds) and never just decorative.

items.name: Da capo architecture
items.description: A section, B section (contrasting, usually more chromatic or in a related minor key), return of A (often with ornamental elaboration). Even in instrumental writing, this ABA thinking shapes the overal

items.name: Sequences that build dramatic momentum
items.description: Sequences (usually descending thirds or circle of fifths) used not just for development but for emotional buildup toward a climax. The sequence intensifies; the resolution releases.

items.name: Dramatic contrast between major and minor
items.description: Handel shifts between parallel major and minor (C major → C minor) for dramatic effect in a way Bach typically does not. A joyful section turning to minor for a sudden shadow, then returning to major

items.name: Sequence as the engine of continuation
items.description: A one- or two-bar figure is restated a step lower (occasionally a step higher) two or three times, usually over a circle-of-fifths bass. This is how a Corelli phrase gets from its opening to its caden

items.name: The suspension chain
items.description: Consecutive 7–6 or 4–3 suspensions between the two upper parts, each resolution preparing the next dissonance. Often welded onto the sequence above, so harmony and dissonance drive forward together.

items.name: A walking bass that is a real line
items.description: The bass moves in steady crotchets or quavers with its own contour and its own cadences, not as chord roots. Under the sequences it walks by fifths; under the cadences it steps.

items.name: Two equal upper voices crossing and exchanging
items.description: The trio-sonata texture: the violins are peers, trade the leading part, cross freely, and move in parallel thirds and sixths for long stretches. Neither is an accompaniment to the other.

items.name: Clear, direct harmony with sudden contrast
items.description: Vivaldi's harmony is functionally clear (I-IV-V), but he deploys sudden moves to the parallel minor or Neapolitan for expressive color — without preparation. The surprise IS the effect.
